arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Ward argued the core liberty interest is freedom from unjustified bodily restraint.
Mr. Clement argued the Court should adopt the subjective test from prior case law.
Justice Kennedy questioned the distinction between discipline and punishment for detainees.
Justice Scalia asked whether the claim relies on substantive due process.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case asks if the Fourteenth Amendment requires a subjective intent standard for pretrial detainees. This differs from the Eighth Amendment standard for convicted prisoners. The lower court applied the subjective test. the side that brought the case seeks an objective standard. the opposing side defends the subjective test.
